cards.text: Israel is OUT of Egypt! On that very day, the LORD brought them out (Exodus 12:51). Now the LORD speaks to Moses, and He's got something to claim as His own.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to consecrate something to Him. What is it?
The LORD says the firstborn of people belong to Him, but not the firstborn of animals.

cards.text: So Moses turns to the people with something they must never forget. And coming from a guy who lost track of what DAY it was for years in a junk drawer? I respect it.

cards.question: What does Moses tell the people to remember?

answers.text: The day they came out of Egypt
The names of the twelve tribes
The night they spent in Goshen

cards.text: Then Moses adds a rule: "And nothing leavened shall be eaten." And he names the month they're leaving in: Abib.

cards.question: Moses names a place where they'll keep this service in this month. Where is it?

answers.text: In the land He swore to their fathers
Back in the land of Goshen
Out in the land of Midian

cards.text: A land flowing with milk and honey, home to the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites and Jebusites. Friend, my old junk drawer was flowing with takeout menus and dead batteries.

cards.question: For ___ days the people eat unleavened bread, and on the last of those days there's a ___ to the LORD.
During those seven days, leaven only has to be kept out of the people's houses.
On that day of the feast, what are the Israelites supposed to do with their sons?

answers.text: Explain what the LORD did for them
Teach them to bake the bread

cards.text: Moses says this will be a sign on their hand and a reminder on their forehead. For with a mighty hand the LORD brought them out of Egypt.

cards.question: Moses says this feast is a one-time thing, just for the year Israel left Egypt.

cards.text: Then Moses comes back to the firstborn. Once they're in the land, every firstborn male goes to the LORD, livestock included.

cards.question: A firstborn donkey gets a different deal. What do they redeem it with?
If a firstborn donkey isn't redeemed, they keep it to work the land.

cards.text: Every firstborn son must be redeemed too, and one day a son will ask, "What does this mean?" Ooh, a story question, and Chip would be FIRST in line.

cards.question: The answer to that son goes all the way back to Egypt. Why do they give the firstborn to the LORD?

answers.text: Because the LORD killed Egypt's firstborn
Because Pharaoh demanded it as payment
Because the firstborn led the march out

cards.text: And then that line again: with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt. A sign on the hand, a symbol on the forehead.
Pharaoh has let the people go, and there's a road through the land of the Philistines. It's the shorter way.

cards.question: God doesn't lead the people on that shorter road through the Philistines' land. Why not?

answers.text: They might face war and turn back
The road ran too close to Pharaoh
The Philistines had closed the road

cards.question: So which way does God lead the people?

answers.text: Through the wilderness toward the Red Sea
East toward the land of Midian
North through the hills of Moab

cards.question: When the Israelites leave Egypt, they're arrayed for battle.

cards.text: And Moses brings something very special along on this trip.

cards.question: What does Moses take with him out of Egypt?
Why does Moses bring Joseph's bones along?

answers.text: Joseph made Israel swear an oath
Aaron was told to in a dream

cards.text: Joseph had said, "God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones with you from this place." And they kept that promise all the way out of Egypt. Friend, I promise to wipe the flour off my mustache, and I forget by the next BATCH.
They set out from Succoth and camp at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

cards.question: Now the LORD goes before the people to guide their way. What does He go before them in by day?
By night, the LORD goes before the people in a pillar of ___ to give them light.

cards.text: Cloud by day, fire by night, so they can travel by day or night. I spent years in a drawer not knowing if it was day or night, and these folks get a NIGHT LIGHT from the LORD!

cards.question: Every now and then, the pillar of cloud leaves its place in front of the people.

cards.text: We'll stop right here at the edge of the wilderness. But hold onto your apron, friend, because this journey is NOT over.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "So Moses turns to the people...", "And coming from a guy who lost track of what DAY it was for years in a junk drawer?" and "I respect it." It is not the opening card, so the limit is 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: Joseph's quote, "And they kept that promise all the way out of Egypt." and the mustache joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer "Joseph made Israel swear an oath" can be read as Joseph making his father Israel (Jacob) swear. Exodus 13:19 says Joseph made "the sons of Israel" swear a solemn oath.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says "keep this service in this month" but never says what the service is. The feast has not been described yet (it comes in 13:6), so "this service" points back to something the baker hasn't been shown and can't see on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card tells the sign on the hand and the reminder on the forehead but leaves out what 13:9 says they are for: "that the Law of the LORD is to be on your lips." No other card covers this, so the meaning of the sign is missed.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Exodus 13:3-16 is Moses' speech, but most of it is rules for a feast (Unleavened Bread) and for offering and redeeming the firstborn. Stop 1 gives it 19 cards, including 11 choice cards on details like seven days and the lamb for a donkey. prep-walkthrough.md lists "rules for offerings and feasts" as a long stretch (one summary card, no choice cards). It also says "speeches, teaching and key laws" are not long stretches. This section fits both.
findings.question: Should a speech made up mostly of feast and offering rules, like Exodus 13:3-16, be treated as a long stretch with one summary card, or as a speech or key law with full story and choice cards?
